subject: MedPoint - short-lived diagnostic logs: temporary retention carveout & evidence pack
messages:
From: Hannah Lee <hannah.lee@medpointhealth.com>
To: security@redwoodinference.com; priyom.das@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Short-lived diagnostic logs - request for temporary retention carveout and evidence

Hi Priyom / Redwood security team,

Quick context: during our integration pilots we've observed a small fraction of requests produce transient errors that require server-side debug traces (full diagnostic request/response + KV cache IDs) to understand root cause. Our compliance group requires an official record showing what we asked for and proof you deleted data afterward.

Could Redwood provide:
- Confirmation of the retention window for diagnostic logs used for customer troubleshooting (we currently see ~7 days in the UI).
- A temporary carveout to retain debug snapshots up to 45 days for our pilot tenants (MedPoint dev/prod), with a clear deletion plan once the pilot ends.
- SIG/CAIQ references or SOC2 evidence that cover ephemeral debug artifacts and deletion proof (we can accept an attestation PDF + sample audit CSV).

We're aiming to close this on our end before the internal security review on 3/2. Appreciate specifics (policy names, locations, and a short evidence pack).

Thanks,
Hannah Lee
CISO (Interim)
MedPoint Health

> Thanks for the note — looping in Priyom (account lead) and our retention SME. We'll review and come back with a proposed carveout and evidence list by early next week.

> — Redwood Security
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Hannah Lee <hannah.lee@medpointhealth.com>
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com, rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Short-lived diagnostic logs - request for temporary retention carveout and evidence

Hannah — thanks for the clear ask. Tagging Neha (security/compliance) and Rishi (platform/runtime) to propose a defensible approach. Internal objectives: keep pilot debugging capability while minimizing blast radius and ensuring auditable deletion.

Proposed immediate steps from our side:
1) Provide a short evidence pack (SIG/CAIQ pointers + SOC2 section references + deletion attestation template).
2) Offer a scoped, timeboxed carveout for MedPoint tenant IDs with strict ACLs and retention TTL = 45 days, accessible only to a named engineering on-call pool and MedPoint's SOC reviewer.
3) Provide a one-off audit CSV listing affected snapshot IDs and a signed deletion confirmation once window ends.

We'll validate technical feasibility (Rishi) and draft the evidence pack (Neha). Expect our follow-up with attachments by Wed 2/18.

Best,
Priyom Das
Enterprise Account Lead | Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwoodinference.com
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Hannah Lee <hannah.lee@medpointhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 08:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Short-lived diagnostic logs - proposed evidence pack and process

Priyom / Hannah — attaching the proposed evidence artifacts for MedPoint's review. Summary below and attachments included: medpoint_sig_answers_20260218.pdf (SIG/CAIQ crosswalk), shortlived-ttl-process-README.md (internal procedure), audit-snapshot-20260218.csv (sample export of snapshot IDs for deletion proof).

Key points:
- Policy: "Ephemeral Debug Artifacts" (internal policy ID: SEC-RI-EPH-003). Default system TTL = 7d. Carveout: tenant-scoped TTL up to 45d for named pilot IDs; must be approved in writing by the account lead + security.
- Access controls: retention buckets are accessible only to redwood:eng-oncall, redwood:security, and a MedPoint SOC group (read-only). All access is logged to the platform audit trail (audit log retention = 1 year).
- Deletion proof: we will produce a CSV export of snapshot IDs, S3 object keys, deletion job run id, and a signed attestation PDF at the end of the retention window.
- Controls to limit exposure: sampling cap (max 5% of pilot traffic can generate snapshot), field redaction for PII by default, and automatic rotation of KMS keys for objects older than 30d.

Attachments: medpoint_sig_answers_20260218.pdf — includes direct SIG control mappings (A.12, A.13 equivalents), and CAIQ references for data lifecycle controls.

Let me know if MedPoint legal wants the deletion attestation to be notarized or if the SOC reviewer needs any additional columns in the audit CSV.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Security & Compliance Lead | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Hannah Lee <hannah.lee@medpointhealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 12:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Short-lived diagnostic logs - proposed evidence pack and process

Hannah — forwarding the package from our compliance team (attached). High level: we can do the 45-day tenant-scoped TTL for the pilot under the controls Neha listed. Implementation notes from Rishi: the carveout will be applied via a tenant tag and is reversible; we'll run a one-time pre-deletion export and then a scheduled delete job (both logged).

Next steps for MedPoint:
- Confirm the pilot tenant IDs and the named MedPoint SOC reviewer (name + email) who needs read access to the audit exports.
- Confirm acceptance of the sampling cap + field redaction defaults.
- Sign the attached short addendum (we can draft) or confirm acceptance via email if DocuSign is not required.

I've included HubSpot ticket HS-55823 and Jira SEC-1227 for tracking.

Thanks,
Priyom
From: Hannah Lee <hannah.lee@medpointhealth.com>

- SOC reviewer: Aaron Blake <aaron.blake@medpointhealth.com> (read-only)

Appreciate the fast turnaround.
